lūdīmăgister (better separately, lūdī măgister ), tri, m. ludus-magister,
I.a school-master, school-teacher: “cum agellus eum non satis aleret, ut opinor, ludi magister fuit,” Cic. N. D. 1, 26, 72 : “Dionysius ludimagistrum professus pueros in trivio docebat,” Just. 21, 5, 8 ; Mart. 10, 62, 1.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
